# Slides

A horizontal, scroll-snapped track of slides with its own arrows and position dots. It is the browser doing the scrolling: the module only watches which slides are in view, through an IntersectionObserver, and moves the track by whole slides when an arrow is used. The arrows step from the slide the snap is resting on, so a track showing three at a time advances by the one in the middle, and the two ends scroll all the way out rather than centering, which is what lines the first and last card up with the page content. Arrows, dots and their states are generated at the end of the component unless the markup already carries them, so writing any of the three yourself is how you place it elsewhere.

## PGS

- `slides`: identifies the root the module initializes, and the element the instance is stored against.
- `slides-container`: the scrolling track, the element that carries the scroll snapping and the one the arrows move. Its measured height is published on the root as --_slides-height and kept in step with it, so a rule can sit something against the slides themselves rather than against the whole component; it is what puts the arrows at the middle of the slides, whatever else the root holds. Read it with a fallback, var(--_slides-height, 100%), for the frame before the first measurement.
- `slides-container-slide`: identifies each direct slide item.
- `slides-prev`: write one yourself, bare like this, to place the previous-slide button elsewhere; the module leaves it alone and never generates a second one.
- `slides-next`: the same, for the next-slide button.
- `slides-dots`: the same, for the row of position dots.

## PGS generated by JavaScript

- `_slides-prev`: appended at the end of the component when no slides-prev was written by hand.
- `_slides-next`: appended at the end of the component when no slides-next was written by hand.
- `_slides-dots`: appended at the end of the component when no slides-dots was written by hand.
- `_slides-dots-dot`: one dot inside the dots row, built and kept in step with the number of slides. It is written on every child of the row, so a row placed by hand holds the same dots.

## PGS Options (component brackets)

- `slidesShadowDesktop`: fades the slides out at the edges from the tablet width up, only on the side that still has slides to reach.
- `slidesAnimationScale`: scales each slide by how much of it is in view, through the --_slides-visiblePercent custom property the module writes on it; a slide sits at 1 before the first pass of the observer.
- `slidesSingleScroll`: an arrow advances by a single slide, counted from the one the snap is resting on, instead of jumping past every slide currently in view.
- `slidesArrowsCenter`: puts the arrows the module builds over the slides again, one on each side at the middle of their height, instead of in a row above them at the end. An arrow written by hand (slides-prev, slides-next) is not moved either way: only the generated ones are.
- `slidesNotDots`: takes the dots off the slides, a row written by hand (slides-dots) included, along with the room kept under the generated one. The module still builds the row, it is only hidden.
- `slidesFullWidth`: each slide fills the full width of the track instead of the default fixed measure, at every breakpoint.
- `slidesLoop`: the prev/next arrows wrap around at the ends instead of stopping, so prev from the first slide goes to the last one and next from the last goes to the first; neither arrow is ever disabled.

## PGS States

- `view`: written on each slide the observer reads as in view, at or above 97% visible. It is what the arrows, the dots and the edge fades are all driven from, and what getCurrentIndexes and getCurrentElements report.
- `active`: written on the dot of each slide currently in view, alongside aria-current.

## JavaScript API

- `pgs.slides.init(root)`: initializes matching elements within the specified root.
- `pgs.slides.api(element)`: returns the instance associated with the specified initialized element.
- `instance.prev()`: moves to the previous slide.
- `instance.next()`: moves to the next slide.
- `instance.goTo(index)`: scrolls to the zero-based slide at that position; throws a TypeError when index is not an integer between 0 and the last slide.
- `instance.getCurrentIndexes()`: returns the positions of every slide currently in view.
- `instance.getCurrentElements()`: returns the slide elements currently in view.
- `instance.getTotal()`: returns the total number of slides.
- `instance.isAtStart()`: returns true when the track is scrolled to its beginning.
- `instance.isAtEnd()`: returns true when the track is scrolled to its end.
- `instance.destroy()`: removes the listeners and observers of the instance and forgets it; the arrows and dots the module generated stay in the markup, and a later init finds and reuses them.
- `instance.refresh()`: destroys the instance and builds a new one on the same element, after the slides have changed, and returns it.

## Related elements

### PGS

- `card`: uses the related card component or utility in this example.
- `card-img`: uses the related card-img component or utility in this example.
- `card-content`: groups the textual content of each slide card.
- `img`: uses the related img component or utility in this example.

### PGS Options (component brackets)

- `imgCover`: inside img's own bracket, crops the image to fill its box.

### Other

- `icon`: draws the chevron inside each of the two generated buttons; see Icon for the whole set.
- `icon-chevronDown`: the glyph in both generated buttons, rotated to point left or right.
- `rotate`: rotates the chevron; the previous button uses its 90 option to point left, the next button its 270 option to point right.
- `btnIconOnly`: styles the previous and next actions generated at runtime; belongs to the button component.

## CSS Variables

- `--slides-maskEnd`
- `--slides-maskStart`
- `--slides-sizeMaskImage`
- `--slides-width`
- `--slides-width-mobile`
- `--slides-width-tablet`

## Examples

### Single scroll

Scrolls to one slide at a time with the prev/next buttons, using pgs=&quot;slides['slidesSingleScroll']&quot;, instead of moving by the full visible width.

```html
<div pgs="slides['slidesSingleScroll']">
    <ul pgs="slides-container">
        <li pgs="slides-container-slide">
            <article pgs="card">
                <img pgs="card-img img['imgCover']" src="../assets/img/placeholder.jpg" alt="Slide 1">
                <div pgs="card-content">
                    <h3>Lorem ipsum dolor</h3>
                    <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.</p>
                </div>
            </article>
        </li>

        <li pgs="slides-container-slide">
            <article pgs="card">
                <img pgs="card-img img['imgCover']" src="../assets/img/placeholder.jpg" alt="Slide 2">
                <div pgs="card-content">
                    <h3>Sit amet consectetur</h3>
                    <p>Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore.</p>
                </div>
            </article>
        </li>

        <li pgs="slides-container-slide">
            <article pgs="card">
                <img pgs="card-img img['imgCover']" src="../assets/img/placeholder.jpg" alt="Slide 3">
                <div pgs="card-content">
                    <h3>Adipiscing elit sed</h3>
                    <p>Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation.</p>
                </div>
            </article>
        </li>
    </ul>
</div>
```

### Arrows over the slides

The arrows the module builds sit in a row above the slides, at the end. slidesArrowsCenter, written as pgs=&quot;slides['slidesArrowsCenter']&quot;, puts them over the slides instead, one on each side at the middle of their height. Arrows written by hand are not moved.
